page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin. The left margin carries no legible text. Below the last line stands the catchword "funt".

main_text.p: quartum: idq; Romanū intelligitur, {a}a o- a melius omniumnibus ante regnis validissimum. Pedes vero partim ferrei, partim fictiles, dividē-ante reg- dum esse Romanum regnum, ita ut nūn.norum quam inter se coeat, praefigurant: quod æ- que impleta est. Siquidem jam non ab u- no imperatore, sed etiam a pluribus, sem- perq; inter se armis aut studiis disentien- tibus, res Romana administratur. Deniq; commisceri testum atq; ferrum nunquam inter se coeuntem materiam; commissiones humani generis futurae, a se invicem disidentes, significantur. Siquidem Romanum solum ab exteris gentibus aut re- bellibus occupatu, aut dedentibus {b}b fem-bfe pér pacis spe- ciem Sig. per pacis specie traditum constat: exerciti. bufque nostris, urbibus atque provinciis permissas barbaras nationes, & praecipue Iudaeos inter nos degere, nec tamen in mores nostros transfire {b}b videamus. videmusAtque haec esse postrema tempora prophetae annunciant. In lapide vero fine manibus abicisso, qui aurum, argentum & ferrum testumq; comminuit, Christi figurā esse. Is enim non conditione humana editus(fiquidem non ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo natus est) mundum iftum, in quo Gij.Iesa. 1.13sunt

page.notes: Marginal reference letters: "a" after "intelligitur," and "b" after "dedentibus" and "transfire" are the text marks; the right margin notes carry them as printed. Right-margin notes "Gij." and "Iesa. 1.13" are uncertain: the latter is read from a worn line and may be [?]. The top-right note reads "a melius" with "omnium" beneath, and the line "a Q-" is uncertain. The word "Romanū" and "ꝑ" forms are read as printed. "Christi figurā" is copied as printed. The final word of the page (sunt) is partly cut at the foot and may be incomplete. The scan is worn at the right edge; the note "Iesa" may be read "Isa." and is marked for checking.
